title: Chapter 35
content:
"There's nothing I can do about it. Father only listens to that bastard Kang Il-hyun."

Resting his forearms along the edge of the pool deck, Kang Seok-joo took a long pull through the straw of a freshly blended watermelon juice a maid had brought out. Even though it was only June, the midday sun blazed with fierce intensity, coating bare skin in a thin sheen of sweat within minutes.

Sitting on the sun lounger, Jakyeong let out a quiet sigh.

With time still left before the scheduled hit, he had tested the waters about staying at the Chairman’s estate until the inauguration, only to be flatly shut down. Chairman Kang claimed Il-hyun had vetoed the move. Seok-joo chalked it up to blatant parental favoritism, but understanding the tangled power struggle underneath, Jakyeong knew the reality was far more twisted.

"Stop brooding and get in. The water feels amazing."

Jakyeong gave a small shake of his head, resting his chin on his crossed arms to stare up at the sky. The stark contrast between the bright crimson patio umbrella and the vast, azure dome above was strikingly vivid. Watching the colors, he set his thoughts of Kang Il-hyun aside and turned his focus to Choi Ki-tae.

Tonight, Ki-tae had chartered an offshore vessel to host an extravagant party on the open water. A "party" in name only—in reality, it was a damage-control operation designed to reassure high-value clients rattled by the explosion at their Doksan-dong processing hub. The ship would serve as an untraceable, floating bazaar for illicit narcotics, lavish entertainment, and backroom syndicate deals.

Judging by his lazy demeanor, Seok-joo was completely in the dark.

Even beneath the shade of the umbrella, the humid heat was oppressive. Jakyeong briefly envied Seok-joo splashing around without a care in the world. As Jakyeong fanned his collar with his fingers, Seok-joo flipped onto his back, floating lazily as his eyes drifted over.

"What's that on your neck?"

"What?"

"The bandage on the side of your neck. Did you get hurt?"

Jakyeong brushed it off with a vague murmur. The deep bruise left behind by Ki-tae’s mouth had refused to fade, leaving him no choice but to cover it with a medical dressing. Having every passing staff member ask about it since sunrise had been exhausting. If it were winter, I could have just thrown on a turtleneck and called it a day.

"Wait... don't tell me...?"

A sleazy, knowing smirk spread across Seok-joo's face as he swam closer. He threw out the name of the high-fashion model from the villa, asking if the two had already hooked up. When Jakyeong denied it, Seok-joo began rattling off the names of every guest Jakyeong had spoken to, completely oblivious to the fact that the culprit was Choi Ki-tae.

"It was just a minor scratch..."

"Right, play innocent all you want."

With an amused chuckle, Seok-joo pushed off the wall and dove back into the deep end. He truly loves the water. Mother aside, in that regard, the kid shared an eerie resemblance to Kang Il-hyun. Whether Il-hyun genuinely enjoyed swimming or simply used the water to nurse the ghost of his late mother remained a mystery.

Tomorrow, Kang Il-hyun would return to Korea.

Jakyeong needed to finish his business tonight and slip back into the estate before the master of the house stepped through the doors. As he took a slow sip of the chilled watermelon juice to beat the heat, his phone chimed.

It was a text from Wang Ryun, confirming the rendezvous time and extraction point.

As Jakyeong typed out his reply, Seok-joo hoisted himself onto the edge of the coping and tapped on the outdoor speakers. Heavy, bass-driven EDM boomed across the flagstones, the aggressive rhythm setting his head bobbing. Jakyeong tapped his index finger against the armrest in time with the tempo, his mind methodically assembling every operational phase for the night ahead.

The erratic coughing sputter of an old engine echoed down the access road, drawing a sharp scowl from the guard stationed outside the main gate.

A battered utility truck had rumbled past a few moments ago, only to stall out fifty yards down the lane, its starter grinding over and over without catching. Losing his patience, the guard marched over to investigate.

He tapped on the driver's side window. A burly man with a buzz cut rolled it down, offering an apologetic grimace.

"Is there a problem here?"

"Ah, the damn engine just died on me out of nowhere."

"Where are you headed?"

The guard’s posture tightened with suspicion. The driver pointed vaguely toward the rolling hills beyond the tree line, where a few scattered farmsteads operated far off the main road. Right on cue, a rank, unmistakable stench of raw livestock manure drifted from the flatbed. The guard pinched his nose in disgust.

"This is strictly private property. Unauthorized vehicles aren't permitted through here."

"Is that so? My apologies, I'm unfamiliar with the area. But look at this mess—the rig won't turn over. Let me pop the hood and take a look."

The driver stepped down and hoisted the heavy steel hood. The guard lingered closely behind his right shoulder, hand hovering near his concealed holster, ready to neutralize any sudden movement.

Leaning over the engine bay, the driver muttered a stream of complaints.

"Ah, the lead came loose. Machines and men—the older they get, the more they fall apart."

He secured the connection and slammed the hood shut with a heavy thud, flashing an easy smile as he climbed back into the cab. He threw the transmission into reverse, executed a three-point turn, and headed back down the mountain road.

Left standing alone in the dust, the guard clicked his tongue in mild annoyance. A sudden hiss broke through his earpiece—Park Tae-soo’s voice checking in on the secure frequency.

[Status report. What was the disturbance?]

"False alarm, sir. Just a lost farm truck making a U-turn."

The guard returned to his post outside the iron gates. Around the perimeter, the mountain air returned to an eerie, breathless silence.

Hidden low in the dense brush fifty yards past the tree line, Jakyeong watched twin headlights cut through the gloom. As the truck slowed to a crawl along the shoulder, he broke from cover, slipping into the passenger seat before anyone could spot his silhouette.

Wang Ryun sat behind the wheel, a satisfied grin on his face. He had orchestrated the mechanical breakdown right on schedule, buying Jakyeong the exact window needed to scale the perimeter wall and vanish into the woods.

"Right on time," Jakyeong murmured.

Ryun let out a heavy, dragging sigh. Looking after half a dozen runaway kids was one thing, but driving an assassin into an unsanctioned, high-risk syndicate hit was giving him an ulcer. Keeping the entire operation hidden from Wang Han only made the weight on his shoulders heavier.

"If Han ever catches wind of this, he’ll skin me alive."

"I'll make it ten percent."

A five percent bump on the spot. The hesitation on Ryun's face vanished instantly, replaced by a massive, ear-to-ear grin.

"Deal. I'll take this secret to my grave."

Swapping vehicles at a predetermined safehouse along the national highway, the two changed out of their work clothes into bespoke evening suits, styling their hair back with pomade. Trading the rusted utility truck for a sleek, high-end imported sedan, they merged onto the expressway, heading straight for the Port of Incheon.

During the drive, Jakyeong reviewed the embossed invitations resting on his lap. The cards were registered to two mid-tier corporate clients—guests his crew had discreetly intercepted and detained for the night to secure their credentials.

"What about the hardware?"

"Stashed in the galley dry-storage bay," Ryun replied, tapping the steering wheel. "Do you have any idea how much grease I had to spread to slip that crate aboard?"

Before Ryun could milk the complaint, Jakyeong raised five fingers in a silent gesture. Another five percent cut—now shut up and drive.

Unlike the cautious Wang Han, Ryun had always possessed a reckless appetite for profit. In that sense, he and Jakyeong had always operated on the same wavelength, which explained why Wang Han had spent their entire youth scolding them both.

As the coastline loomed into view, Jakyeong slid a pair of dark sunglasses onto the bridge of his nose.

Rows of luxury vehicles were already lining the private pier. At the base of the boarding ramp, Ki-tae’s security detail—sharp-suited enforcers with earpieces—were methodically checking credentials and conducting physical pat-downs.

Unlike standard attendees, high-profile VIPs bypassed the search entirely, gliding aboard with a simple flash of their black invitations.

After parking in a discreet bay, Jakyeong and Ryun joined the queue of guests in formal attire. Through the crowd, Jakyeong spotted Choi Ki-tae standing near the gangway, though fortunately, the man was entirely occupied bowing and laughing with a circle of VIP guests.

Keeping his back angled away from Ki-tae, Jakyeong stepped up to the checkpoint. An enforcer verified their names on the master registry, then held out a clear security pouch, politely requesting their personal devices, which would be returned upon docking. Handing over their pre-configured burner phones, the enforcers tagged the bag and conducted a thorough physical pat-down.

Passing the scan without a hitch, they were handed their stateroom keycards.

At the threshold, a hostess pinned a gleaming gold guest badge to their lapels. The chartered vessel was a full-scale luxury cruise liner—far more opulent and expansive than anticipated. Stepping into the grand atrium, an enormous crystal chandelier hung suspended from the vaulted ceiling.

The amenities spanned multiple levels: indoor plunge pools, thermal spas, private gaming salons, a theater, and an open-air sundeck complete with a putting green. The upper decks were reserved exclusively for private suites.

Around the atrium, well-dressed guests were already mingling with drinks in hand. As Jakyeong scanned the room to map the exits, Ryun reached toward a passing server's tray to grab a flute of champagne.

Jakyeong intercepted his wrist, setting the glass firmly back down.

"Don't touch it."

"Just one glass."

"That glass could be the last thing you drink on this earth. Keep your head on straight."

"Always so strict," Ryun muttered, though he pulled his hand back.

Pretending to take in the lavish decor, they mapped the interior corridors, the placement of private security stations, and the approximate headcount of armed crew members before heading up to their assigned cabin.

Ascending the grand staircase, Jakyeong paused on the mezzanine landing.

The central ballroom was visible below, packed with an even larger crowd of revelers. Scanning the room, his gaze locked onto Choi Ki-tae's father, Choi Moon-sung.

The old man looked remarkably different from the broken, grieving father at the temple days ago; his hair was dyed an immaculate jet-black, radiating energy and vigor. Draped in an expensive suit with a stunning young woman on his arm, he moved through the room exchanging handshakes and laughter.

Ryun nudged Jakyeong’s elbow, gesturing discreetly with his chin. "That him?"

"Yeah."

"Look at him enjoying the spotlight... having no clue tonight is his final memorial service."

Jakyeong offered no comment.

Turning away from the railing, he tapped their keycard against the electronic lock. The stateroom featured two twin beds and an en-suite bath. Resting on the bedside console was a complimentary tray of imported cannabis joints and assorted designer pills.

Ryun sank onto the mattress with a low chuckle. "You know, Jakyeong... sitting here like this, it almost feels like we're on our honeymoon."

Removing his dark glasses, Jakyeong strode over to the porthole.

Through the thick glass, the dark sea stretched out to meet the horizon. Far in the distance, the lanterns of commercial fishing trawlers flickered against the water, drawing deep-sea prey toward the surface.

Jakyeong placed a cigarette between his lips, and Ryun immediately stepped up to offer a flame.

Exhaling a stream of pale smoke against the cold glass, Jakyeong stared out into the pitch-black water. The dark irises of his eyes slowly sank into the void, turning as cold and fathomless as the sea itself.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Floating Drug Operations (선상 파티): Hosting high-stakes narcotics distribution and gambling rings aboard chartered vessels in international or territorial waters is a classic underworld tactic, exploiting jurisdictional grey areas and strict access control to keep operations completely hidden from domestic coast guard sweeps.

  • Memorial Day / Jesa (제삿날): In Korean culture, Jesa is the traditional ancestral memorial ritual held on the anniversary of a person's death. Ryun using the phrase "his final jesat-nal" is a dark, colloquial idiom meaning "the day he dies."
